A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same spectrally guided diffusion work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, comparisons with reproduced SiD2 models, sampling-step evaluations, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original text-to-image, unconditional generation, high-step degradation, contrast-control, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The core spectral schedules and training/sampling algorithms remain unchanged. v2 implements text conditioning through T5-XXL embeddings, pooled FiLM conditioning, and transformer cross-attention, with an attention-pooling/MLP spectrum sampler (Sections 4.4, 5.5, and D.2). These are adaptations of the retained method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates class-conditional ImageNet generation. v2 adds text-conditioned training on the dataset described as SiD2's, zero-shot MS-COCO evaluation at 512 × 512, and unconditional ImageNet generation at 256 × 256. These substantially broaden task and distribution coverage.

E2.justification: The original class-conditional comparator sets remain unchanged. New comparisons include published SiD text-to-image results in Table 3 and ADM unconditional results in Table 5, alongside SiD2.

E3.justification: v2 adds zero-shot text evaluation, baseline sampling sweeps extending to 4096 steps, a gamma = 0.5 sampling control, and timed hardware comparisons. Appendix D.2 also revises the reported class-conditional sampler from 3 to 5 mixture components and learning rate 0.001 to 0.01. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 newly investigates high-step degradation using multiple metrics, extended SiD2 sampling, and increased sampling noise. Section 5.5 adds a text-to-image oracle-spectrum comparison, while Appendix C.2 demonstrates contrast manipulation previously only described. Original schedule, conditioning, and hyperparameter ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging the main ImageNet results over five generation sets with different seeds. v2 introduces no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: All original table entries and Figure 3 curves are retained. New results include MS-COCO FID 7.08 at 96 steps versus reproduced SiD2's 7.56 at 160 steps, and unconditional ImageNet FID 16.8 at 256 steps versus 17.2 at 512 steps. Table 4 adds degradation and noise-control results; Appendix E adds measured runtime results. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The spectral bounds and closed-form schedule derivations are retained. Added substitution steps and the explicit least-squares objective elaborate existing computations. The expectation qualification was already present in v1's derivation, and the Parseval explanation formalizes its existing spectrum–variance connection rather than introducing a substantive new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same scientific claims. The introduction's fourth numbered contribution becomes a separate paragraph with unchanged meaning. Additional experiments support the existing efficiency and generative-quality claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds diversity-loss and model-strength hypotheses for high-step degradation, attributes the text-to-image oracle advantage to distribution shift, and explicitly identifies the mixed schedule as heuristic. One interpretation is overstated: Appendix C.1 claims the gamma = 0.5 variant beats SiD2 at every step count, but Table 4 gives FID 2.99 versus 2.96 at 128 steps.

D1.justification: v2 documents text-conditioning architecture, sampler dimensions and hyperparameters, additional FiLM/guidance explanations, parallel RAPSD preprocessing, TPU hardware, and training/inference timings. It also revises the class-sampler settings. Reproducibility information expands substantially, although the text-training dataset remains identified only through the SiD2 reference.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for ADM, MS-COCO, attention pooling, and T5, supporting its new experiments and implementation. The main positioning against global noise schedules and earlier spectral approaches remains unchanged. The Ramesh citation-year correction concerns the same work.

P1.justification: v2 locally clarifies schedule construction, spectrum manipulation, and conditioning, and corrects wording. It adds Section 5.5 and an impact statement, subdivides Appendix C, and inserts a computational-cost appendix. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds dedicated text-to-image, high-step degradation, and unconditional comparison tables, plus contrast-control and text-to-image sample grids. Existing displays are retained, with Table 1 highlighting and some relocation. Original appendix Tables 3–5 become Tables 6–8, and the original sample Figure 6 becomes Figure 7.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical support was confined to class-conditional ImageNet and left high-step deterioration unexplained. v2 substantially strengthens the paper through cross-task validation, diagnostic experiments testing a mitigation for that deterioration, and measured runtime evidence supporting practical efficiency. Incomplete text-data disclosure, unexplained revisions to sampler settings, and the overstated all-step comparison limit reproducibility and interpretation, but do not outweigh these substantial gains.
